22 A longitudinal wave travelling from left to right has vibrations parallel to the direction of transfer of
energy by the wave.
The wave can be represented on a graph showing the variation with distance of the displacement
of the particles from their equilibrium positions at one instant.
Which point on the graph is the centre of a compression?
direction of
transfer of energy
A
displacement
to the right
B
D
0
0
distance
from source
displacement
to the left
C

hints: Look at the axes: vertical is particle displacement to the right or left, horizontal is distance from source, and energy transfer is left to right.
Recall a compression means particles on both sides are displaced toward the same central position, while a rarefaction means they are displaced away from it.
Compare the zero-crossings B and D: check whether the curve goes from positive to negative or negative to positive and what that says about particles either side.
walkthrough: The graph shows at one instant the longitudinal displacement $x$ of each particle against its equilibrium distance from the source. Up means displaced to the right, down means displaced to the left.
A compression is a region of high particle density where particles on the left have moved right and particles on the right have moved left, meeting at the centre where net displacement is zero.

At B the curve crosses zero going downwards. Just left of B displacement is positive, so particles are to the right of equilibrium. Just right of B displacement is negative, so particles are to the left of equilibrium.
Both sets of particles are therefore pushed toward the position of B, increasing the local density. This is the cause-and-effect signature of a compression.

At D the curve crosses zero going upwards, with left-side particles displaced left and right-side particles displaced right, so they spread apart in a rarefaction. Points A and C are displacement maxima, not zero crossings.
Therefore the centre of a compression is the downward zero crossing. This is option B.

A.explanation: Point A is maximum displacement to the right. Neighbouring particles are also displaced to the right, so it is not where particles crowd together.

B.explanation: At B the displacement is zero with particles to the left displaced right and particles to the right displaced left, so they move toward B and form a compression.

C.explanation: Point C is maximum displacement to the left. It is a point of large displacement, not the zero-displacement crossing where crowding occurs.

D.explanation: At D the displacement is zero but particles to the left are displaced left and to the right are displaced right, so they spread apart in a rarefaction.
